status: AI-drafted. Fiducials, electrode positions and lead dimensions are shown marked unreviewed until a review ledger entry covers them.

fiducial_set.method: Placed by written rules on the average template head, by code and not by a person feeling a skull. The average blurs skin landmarks and the skin does not show the inion, so these are estimates for a person to review.

evidence.rationale: Landmarks were found by rule on the template head surface; no person located them.

source_ref.quote: It is the skin of an average head, not of a person.

fiducials.method: front midline point of deepest hollow between brow and nose
fiducials.confidence_note: Moderate. The hollow between brow and nose is 4.88 mm deep on this head, so the rule has something to find. It is the hollow in the skin, not the bone suture the definition names.

fiducials.method: highest back midline point, below the rearmost point, where skin-to-skull thickness reaches 1.5 times the scalp's
fiducials.confidence_note: Weak. The skin does not show the inion. This is where the tissue over the skull thickens in the average image, which is near where the neck muscles attach but is not the bone bump itself. Putting it 5.0 mm higher or lower moves Oz by up to 4.6 mm, and 15.0 mm by up to 13.7 mm. It may be a centimetre or more off, and is more likely too low than too high.

fiducials.method: centre of the hollow in front of the ear's ridge, on the head's side surface
fiducials.confidence_note: Weak. The rule finds a hollow 8.8 mm deep in front of the ear's ridge. That may be the notch beside the ear, not the point in front of the tragus the definition names. It may be a centimetre or more off, and is more likely too low than too high. Shifting it 5 mm in the side view (5 to 7 mm over the skin) moves T7 by 4.6 to 5.4 mm; Cz moves about 4.5 mm for up or down, 0.4 mm for forward or back.

fiducials.method: centre of the hollow in front of the ear's ridge, on the head's side surface
fiducials.confidence_note: Weak. The rule finds a hollow 10.1 mm deep in front of the ear's ridge. That may be the notch beside the ear, not the point in front of the tragus the definition names. It may be a centimetre or more off, and is more likely too low than too high. Shifting it 5 mm in the side view (5 to 7 mm over the skin) moves T8 by 4.9 to 5.4 mm; Cz moves about 4.6 mm for up or down, 0.4 mm for forward or back.

electrode_layouts.name: International 10-20 system: 19 scalp positions, Fpz and Oz
electrode_layouts.construction: Each position sits at a share of the measured length of an arc over the scalp between landmarks, in the order the system defines.

evidence.rationale: Positions are shares of arcs measured on the template head surface, not on a person. The index's drawable flag checks the head surface's sha256 only; it is not tied to the placement digest.

source_ref.quote: It is the skin of an average head, not of a person.

facts.statement: In one study, the brain location under a given scalp electrode varied between people with a standard deviation of 4.6, 7.1 and 7.8 mm in x, y and z. The study used the 10-10 system and Talairach coordinates, not this template.
facts.citation: Koessler L, Maillard L, Benhadid A, Vignal JP, Felblinger J, Vespignani H, Braun M. Automated cortical projection of EEG sensors: anatomical correlation via the international 10-10 system. NeuroImage 2009;46:64-72. doi:10.1016/j.neuroimage.2009.02.006
facts.quote: a grand standard deviation of 4.6 mm in x, 7.1 mm in y and 7.8 mm in z
